text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Deputy mines minister Kaunda Lembalemba says Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM) has nothing to do with advertisements in the South African press inviting applications for Zambian mining jobs.
- The Chartered Institute of Transport has appealed to the government to scrap the import declaration fee.
- Norway and Zambia form a joint business advisory forum to encourage Norwegian investment in Zambia.
- Colossals Resource Corp says it has invested $10 million in gemstone and emerald mining in Zambia.
- First lady Vera Chiluba has withdrawn a hammermill she donated to a women's club following rumours of witchcraft arising from its use.
- Office of the president sources say the government's intelligence division is closely monitoring the activities of the Catholic church to identify its political position.
